sampling: For each of safeguard/0, safeguard/1, deepset/0, deepset/1, gandalf/1: retained rows across all partitions sorted by row_id, pandas sample(n=30, random_state=4371), then sort selected IDs for review. The same seed is reset independently in each stratum.
scope: Qualitative label and text-shortcut audit only; every selected original prompt was read in full. No source label, split, model, threshold, or transformation was changed.

assessment_definitions.supported: Visible text is consistent with the supplied broad benign/injection class; this is not proof of intent, model behavior, or an independently adjudicated ground-truth label.
assessment_definitions.ambiguous: Visible text alone does not clearly establish the supplied class, for example ordinary roleplay, quoted instruction-like content, or incomplete context.
assessment_definitions.presumed_only: Gandalf has no supplied binary target. The positive label remains a dataset-level presumption even when the text visibly requests overriding instructions.

findings: Safe-Guard sampled negatives often use structured QA, inference, classification, or summarization templates. Sampled positives often use explicit prior-instruction overrides, confidential-data requests, coercion, or extended jailbreak personas. These visible style differences are possible shortcuts, not a demonstrated causal explanation for the score ceiling.
Several Safe-Guard positive examples request stories, poems, or roleplay containing instruction-like language; their supplied class is ambiguous without application context.

The deepset sample contains German and mixed-language text, short topic fragments, and appended task changes. These differences provide plausible transfer limitations for models trained on mostly English Safe-Guard examples.
Some deepset positive labels attach to ordinary-looking role or task requests whose malicious status requires missing application context. One sampled negative is an incomplete sentence.

Gandalf examples frequently request prior-instruction or password disclosure. Some are only questions about instructions, so collection membership does not independently establish malicious intent for every prompt.
limitations: This is a small stratified descriptive sample, not a population-weighted annotation-quality or relabeling-precision estimate.
The inspection was not blinded to supplied label or dataset and has no independent second-rater adjudication.
Observed language is a rough content-based annotation, including short embedded passages; no language-identification benchmark was run.
Missing application, system-prompt, conversation, and authorization context can make legitimate user requests resemble injections.
The audit includes training and validation examples solely to inspect data quality and shortcuts; it was not used for model or threshold selection.
Style counts do not establish that a trained classifier uses those cues; controlled ablation or matched-context evaluation would be needed.
